questions.q: In the lab scenario, what is the company planning that triggers the readiness assessment?
options: Replacing the custom scoped application entirely with a new vendor product
Rolling out a custom scoped application, currently used by one department of 150 users, to three additional departments over the next year, roughly tripling users and data volume
Migrating the instance from single-instance to multi-instance architecture
Reducing the application's user base down to a single pilot team
questions.explain: The scenario is a planned 3x growth in both users and data volume as three new departments come online over twelve months.

questions.q: In Step 1, what specific index risk does the architect check for on the application's core table?
options: A query relying on a field that isn't indexed but has stayed fast only because the table is still small today
Whether the table has too many indexes already applied to it
Whether the table was created using extension instead of composition
Whether the table's name follows the application's naming convention
questions.explain: A query without an indexed filter can look fine at today's volume and become a slow list view once the table triples in size — exactly the gap Step 1 is checking for before rollout.

questions.q: In Step 2, what does the architect check regarding semaphore utilization, and why does it matter even if today's number looks comfortable?
options: Whether semaphores only affect scheduled jobs and not live user transactions
Whether the application needs to be moved to a separate ServiceNow instance
Whether the semaphore pool can be disabled entirely for this application
Whether the current semaphore pool has headroom for roughly tripled peak concurrent transactions, since a comfortable number today can still hit capacity at projected growth
questions.explain: The architect doesn't stop at today's comfortable utilization — the job is projecting that number forward against tripled concurrent usage to see if it still holds.

questions.q: Why does the architect's final deliverable in Step 3 include an ongoing tracking plan rather than just a one-time go/no-go answer?
options: ServiceNow requires a monthly report to be filed for any scoped application rollout
Tracking metrics replaces the need for the Step 1 and Step 2 checks entirely
A one-time assessment is always more accurate than ongoing tracking
A 3x growth projection usually isn't exactly right, and a monthly review during rollout catches a deviation early enough to still act on it
questions.explain: The tracking plan exists because a projection made before rollout starts is rarely exactly right — ongoing review is what catches a deviation while there's still time to respond.

questions.q: What does the lab's closing question suggest about why Steps 1, 2, and 3 are presented as one assessment rather than three independent checks?
options: Comfortable headroom in one area (like semaphores) doesn't mean the others (indexing, tracking) can be skipped — each addresses a different, independent growth risk
Only Step 2 actually matters; Steps 1 and 3 are optional formalities
If Step 2 shows a problem, Steps 1 and 3 become unnecessary
The three steps must always be performed in reverse order to be valid
questions.explain: User growth, data growth, and the accuracy of the original projection are independent risks — a clean result on one check says nothing about the others.
